dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.lead: The form is the brief. The server compiles the prompt, plans the cut and renders a file. A silent cut needs no API key.
dashboard.newVideoHelp: Hover or focus the info icons for how to fill each field.

tips.goal: What the viewer should think, feel or do after watching. One sentence, one outcome: "Get neighbors to visit the Saturday market".
tips.audience: Who watches, in plain words: "parents of toddlers in Lisbon". A specific audience sets the vocabulary, the pace and the hook.
tips.subject: The one thing the video is about, or the offer. If you need "and" twice, split it into two videos.
tips.duration: Length in seconds, 5 to 300. Short vertical videos hold attention best at 15 to 45 seconds; cut anything that does not earn its time.
tips.ratio: Frame shape. 9:16 for Reels, Shorts and TikTok (keep text and faces inside the safe area, away from the top and bottom UI). 1:1 and 4:5 for feeds, 16:9 for YouTube and the web.
tips.style: The visual recipe the planner follows: shot types, pacing and captions. Pick the one closest to the tone you want.
tips.language: Language of the voice and captions, as a code such as en or pt. Captions matter: most people watch with the sound off.
tips.facts: Claims the video must keep, one per line: prices, dates, names, numbers. The planner will not invent or change them.
tips.links: Pages with extra context, such as the product page or an article. They are references for you and the plan, not downloaded footage.
tips.cta: The single action at the end: "Visit studio.example". Say it once, say it plainly, and keep it on screen long enough to read.
tips.voice: Silent needs nothing and relies on captions. Local text to speech reads the script on this server. Upload a WAV to use your own recording.
tips.music: Name the license or source of the music bed, such as "Pixabay 123". Leave it empty to ship without music; never use tracks you cannot license.
tips.voiceFile: A WAV recording of the narration. Record in a quiet room, close to the microphone, and keep it close to the chosen duration.

tips.title: Tips
tips.lead: Short rules for good short videos.

hook.text: Open on the payoff, a question or motion. No logo, no greeting.

oneIdea.text: A single message and a single call to action at the end.

captions.text: Most people scroll with sound off. Keep lines short and high contrast.

pacing.text: Change the picture every 2-4 seconds for fast content; hold longer to let a detail land.

safeArea.text: In 9:16, keep text and faces away from the top and bottom, where app buttons sit.

loudness.text: Master the mix near -14 LUFS (about -1 dBTP peak) so platforms do not turn you down.

thirds.text: Place the subject on a third line, not the centre; leave look room in the direction they face.

shots.text: Wide sets the place, medium carries the action, close-up shows emotion or a detail. Mix them.

jl.text: Let the audio of the next shot start before the picture (J) or the previous audio run over it (L). It smooths cuts.

broll.text: Cover talking or text with relevant footage to hide jump cuts and show what you describe.

colour.text: Use one look across shots: same white balance and contrast, a small palette.

audio.text: Viewers forgive soft picture, not bad sound. Record close, cut silences, duck music under voice.
